key_insight: ActCam enables zero-shot joint control of actor motion and per-frame camera parameters, transferring performance from a driving video into a new scene by conditioning a pretrained image-to-video diffusion model on depth and motion.
problem_solved: Provides fine-grained, joint control over both character performance and cinematography without task-specific training, addressing the gap between motion transfer and explicit camera trajectory control in video generation.
method: Zero-shot pipeline built on pretrained image-to-video diffusion models (no finetuning required).
Extracts per-frame motion/pose from a driving video and conditions generation on scene depth + motion to transfer the actor into a target scene.
Enables per-frame intrinsic and extrinsic camera parameter conditioning to produce consistent, editable camera trajectories alongside the transferred performance.
impact: Enables artists and ML practitioners to create cinematic, controllable videos quickly for content creation, prototyping, and data augmentation, lowering the barrier to advanced motion-and-camera-aware synthesis.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: inputs (driving video + target scene) → pose & depth extraction → conditioned diffusion model → output video

paper_title: ActCam: Zero-Shot Joint Camera and 3D Motion Control for Video Generation
paper_authors: Omar El Khalifi, Thomas Rossi, Oscar Fossey, Thibault Fouque, Ulysse Mizrahi
